messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] half -cauchy prior
parts:
Finn

On 15 Feb 2017, at 21:25, Belay Birlie <belaya...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear All

After having a look at the documentation and discussion board, I try to implement half-Cauchy Prior but it gives me the following error. 

Error in inla.model.properties.generic(inla.trim.family(model), (mm[names(mm) == : Name 'expressiion:' is unknown. Valid choices are: normal gaussian wishart1d wishart2d wishart3d wishart4d wishart5d loggamma minuslogsqrtruncnormal logtnormal logtgaussian flat logflat logiflat mvnorm pcar none invalid betacorrelation logitbeta pcprec pcdof pccor0 pccor1 pcfgnh pcspdega pcmatern pcrange pc refar jeffreystdf expression: table


Perhaps a silly observation, but "expressiion:" should be "expression:"?

Finn


My code

# Generate Poisson Data
nyy<-30
n.sub<-30
ti<-seq(from=0,to=1,length=nyy)
mu.i<-pi*cos(16*ti)
mu.i<-mu.i+abs(min(mu.i))+6
min(mu.i)
dat.mat.1<-dat.mat.2<-matrix(0,n.sub,nyy)
sig.a<-0.75
a.i<-rnorm(n.sub,0,sig.a)
for(i in 1:n.sub)
{
dat.mat.1[i,]<-mu.i+a.i[i]
dat.mat.2[i,]<-rpois(nyy,mu.i+a.i[i])
}

# prepare the generated data for modeling
y<-c(dat.mat.2[1,]) # responce
for (i in 2:n.sub){y=c(y,dat.mat.2[i,])}

time<-c(rep(ti,n.sub))
id<-rep(1:n.sub,each=nyy)
Simdata<-data.frame(id,time,y)



## implementing the loggamma-prior using "expression:"
loggamma = "expression:
a = 1;
b = 0.1;
precision = exp(log_precision);
logdens = log(b^a) - lgamma(a)
+ (a-1)*log_precision - b*precision;
log_jacobian = log_precision;
return(logdens + log_jacobian);"

hyper.new1 = list(prec = list(prior = loggamma))

## implementing the half-cauchy using "expression:"

loghc = "expressiion:
prec = exp(theta);
scale = 25;
ld = -log(pi * scale) -log(1 + (prec/scale)^2);
logjac = theta;
return(ld + logjac);"

hyper.new2 = list(prec = list(prior = loghc))

## Incorporating them in to our model...

formula1=y~time+f(id,model="iid",hyper = hyper.new1)

formula2=y~time+f(id,model="iid",hyper = hyper.new2)

r1 = inla(formula1, data = Simdata,
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),family="poisson",control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE))
r2 = inla(formula2, data = Simdata,
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),family="poisson",control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE))



print(r1$summary.hyperpar[1,"mean"])
print(r2$summary.hyperpar[1,"mean"])
